# DATP Journal Extension — Authoritative Roadmap-to-Code Audit Matrix

> **EXTRACTION ONLY.** This document is a roadmap-derived scientific audit specification. It does **not** audit the current implementation, does **not** inspect production code, does **not** fix anything, and does **not** reinterpret the roadmap to match code.

> Historical opaque threshold/regime aliases used by the source roadmap have been translated throughout this matrix to descriptive scientific identities such as `CENTRALIZED_REFERENCE`, `SHARED_THRESHOLD`, `LOCAL_THRESHOLD`, `FAMILY_THRESHOLD`, `CLUSTER_THRESHOLD`, `NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES`, `CICIOT_FILE_CLIENTS`, `NBAIOT_DIRICHLET_CLIENTS`, `EDGE_SENSOR_GROUPS`, and `EDGE_TEMPORAL_GROUPS`. Source line numbers preserve traceability to the authoritative roadmap.

## 2. Scientific programme contract

### Central research question

When heterogeneous IoT clients share one frozen federated anomaly detector, determine how the **scope of benign threshold calibration** changes the **distribution of false-alarm burden across clients**. The primary scientific object is cross-client FPR dispersion; AUROC is a detector-quality control, not the threshold-policy verdict.

### Manipulated variable

`threshold_calibration_scope`, with the core descriptive states `SHARED_THRESHOLD`, `FAMILY_THRESHOLD`, `CLUSTER_THRESHOLD`, and `LOCAL_THRESHOLD`.

### Causal unit

The controlled causal comparison is **within one training seed, one dataset/population regime, one training baseline, and one frozen detector**. The independent replication unit for inference is the **training seed**.

### Evidence architecture

| Evidence tier | Roadmap contract |
| --- | --- |
| Confirmatory | Only N-BaIoT `NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES`, `SHARED_THRESHOLD` versus `LOCAL_THRESHOLD`, `CV(FPR)`, ten paired training seeds, and the locked paired BCa decision rule. |
| Supportive | Robustness/sensitivity checks that may narrow or reinforce interpretation but cannot replace the confirmatory endpoint. |
| Mechanism | Explains calibration granularity, score geometry, distribution heterogeneity, cluster stability, threshold movement, and training-side absorption; associative/descriptive unless explicitly otherwise. |
| External | Edge-IIoTset `EDGE_SENSOR_GROUPS` validates benign operating-point equity only; attack-sensitive per-client external evidence is unavailable by design. |
| Stress-test | FedProx and Ditto change the detector/training state and therefore must remain outside the threshold-only causal ladder. |
| Boundary | CICIoT2023 file pseudo-clients, calibration-size limits, and one-shot temporal recalibration identify applicability/robustness boundaries. |
| Exploratory | Alternative cluster counts, optional cluster median, additional equity indices, fixed-k summary sensitivity, and similar optional analyses cannot be post-hoc promoted. |

### MUST remain fixed
- Selected autoencoder/detector state within a core threshold comparison.
- Named fitted preprocessing state and normalization semantics.
- Client identities and population membership.
- Predefined data partitions/splits.
- Benign calibration records, except only where a declared calibration-size/future-recalibration experiment intentionally changes them.
- Held-out test scores and labels.
- Eligibility rule and eligible client population.
- Canonical quantile target except in the declared quantile-sensitivity experiment.
- Metric formulas/implementation and score comparison operator.
- Model family, architecture contract, FedAvg training algorithm, one local epoch per round, full participation, training hyperparameters, round/checkpoint candidate protocol, seed cohort, scoring procedure, and test population within the core ladder.

### MAY vary
- Threshold-calibration scope in the core ladder.
- Quantile only inside the pre-specified quantile-sensitivity grid.
- Shrinkage coefficient only inside the pre-specified shrinkage grid; size-aware shrinkage only under a pre-specified function.
- CLUSTER_THRESHOLD cluster count only in explicitly exploratory/supplementary granularity sensitivity; canonical K remains 3.
- Training method only in separate stress tests with separate detectors/scores/evaluations.
- Dataset/population only when the experiment explicitly changes regime/evidence role.
- Calibration subsample size only in the calibration-size ablation and nested replicates.
- Future threshold state only in the declared one-shot temporal recalibration experiment.

### MUST differ when the experiment changes the scientific object
- `CENTRALIZED_REFERENCE` must use an independently trained centralized model and centralized preprocessing state; FedAvg scores cannot be relabelled.
- FedProx and Ditto stress tests must use independently trained detector states and separate score artifacts from FedAvg.
- Different incompatible dataset feature spaces require dataset-specific model parameters/input dimensions.
- Different named preprocessing protocol identities are scientifically different conditions and may not be mixed silently.

### MUST NOT influence the comparison
- Held-out test F1, TPR, AUROC, balanced accuracy, CV(FPR), or other test outcomes may not select thresholds, q, lambda, mu, K, client eligibility, checkpoint, or policy.
- Attack-labelled records may not influence threshold values, quantile selection, eligibility, checkpoint selection, comparator tuning, shrinkage strength, conformal alpha, cluster count/features, or external client construction.
- Expected policy ordering may not determine client inclusion, seed inclusion, checkpoint choice, or whether a mandatory experiment is reported.
- External/stress-test outcomes may not select core confirmatory parameters.

### MUST NOT be claimed
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-001:** The study establishes which model or federated-learning algorithm is best. — The scientific question is threshold-calibration scope under fixed detector.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-002:** LOCAL_THRESHOLD improves AUROC. — Threshold changes cannot change score ranking under fixed scores.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-003:** DATP improves detection performance overall. — Macro-F1/lower-tail metrics may weaken; primary object is FPR dispersion.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-004:** DATP/threshold personalization improves every client or every metric. — Roadmap explicitly allows trade-offs and negative outcomes.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-005:** DATP is privacy preserving or provides a formal privacy guarantee. — No formal privacy mechanism/guarantee is implemented.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-006:** CLUSTER_THRESHOLD is a privacy mechanism. — Explicitly excluded.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-007:** Estimated message sizes prove deployment feasibility, edge readiness, or light weight. — No hardware/network/energy/latency validation.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-008:** The study validates fleet-scale behavior above 100 clients. — No such real fleet validation; synthetic/pseudo-clients do not establish it.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-009:** The study is a complete FL-IDS framework benchmark or broad FL benchmark. — Scope is bounded.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-010:** The study solves non-IID federated learning. — It studies threshold scope and bounded stress tests.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-011:** The study establishes state of the art, universal superiority, or a first-of-kind novelty claim. — Independent evidence beyond roadmap would be required.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-012:** Edge-IIoTset validates per-client attack detection, TPR, Macro-F1, BA, AUROC, or attack-sensitive equity. — Valid per-client attack assignment is unavailable.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-013:** A CICIoT2023 pseudo-client result generalizes to the original 105 physical devices. — Available artifact lacks verified physical-device mapping.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-014:** CICIoT2023 file-defined clients are physical devices. — Physical mapping absent; artificial groups prohibited.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-015:** Generated pseudo-time can stand in for real chronology. — Explicitly prohibited.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-016:** One-shot temporal recalibration handles concept drift, continuous adaptation, online learning, or streaming drift detection. — Temporal scope is one bounded recalibration window.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-017:** FEDERATED_BENIGN_SUMMARY_STATISTICS_THRESHOLD is a faithful Laridi reproduction. — Laridi uses anomalous validation summaries; DATP comparator excludes them.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-018:** A failed confirmatory endpoint can be rescued by CLUSTER_THRESHOLD, shrinkage, conformal, external, or exploratory evidence. — Evidence tiers cannot be promoted post hoc.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-019:** FedProx or Ditto is another threshold-scope condition in the core ladder. — They change detector/training state.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-020:** A fallback personalized method may be called Ditto without genuine Ditto semantics. — Naming must match actual algorithm.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-021:** LOCAL_SPLIT_CONFORMAL_THRESHOLD proves arbitrary client-conditional coverage or validity under unrestricted non-exchangeability/adversarial calibration. — Roadmap restricts it to an empirical bounded diagnostic.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-022:** Identity/no-scaling preprocessing is a confirmatory multi-feature AE input option. — Explicitly excluded.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-023:** A policy parameter, checkpoint, q, lambda, mu, cluster count, or client set may be selected using held-out test outcomes. — Test-based tuning is prohibited.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-024:** Undefined/unavailable metrics may be represented as zero, empty values, inherited values, or unqualified NaN. — Typed unavailability with reason is mandatory.
- **FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-025:** Unfavorable seeds, clients, null results, reversed results, or infeasible results may be hidden or removed. — Negative-result discipline requires reporting them.

### Non-operative numeric occurrence register

These occurrences were inspected during the dedicated number pass but do **not** define scientific execution values. They are retained only to prove that raw numeric text was not silently ignored.

Number words such as “one”, “two”, “three”, “four”, “five”, “nine”, and “ten” were inspected separately. Where they define a scientific count/scope (for example one local epoch, nine clients, ten seeds, one new dataset, two stress tests), they are represented above. Where they are ordinary grammar (“one of the following”), procedural rhetoric, or duplicate restatements of an already locked count, they are non-operative prose.

## 6. Dataset matrix

### DATASET-NBAIOT — N-BaIoT
| Field | Roadmap-derived contract |
| --- | --- |
| Scientific role | Sole confirmatory dataset anchor; also controlled-heterogeneity and mechanism/stress-test substrate. |
| Available data semantics | Nine physical IoT devices; original study context includes Mirai and BASHLITE; physical devices are natural clients. |
| Client identity / permissible populations | NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES (9 natural physical clients); NBAIOT_DIRICHLET_CLIENTS (20 synthetic clients); dataset-specific centralized pooled reference. |
| Forbidden population constructions | Synthetic clients cannot replace natural-device evidence; no fleet-scale inference from nine clients; no client filtering for favorable pattern. |
| Feature requirements | Declared feature schema/dimension for N-BaIoT is ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED. Non-finite declared features fail validation; no filling/imputation. |
| Label requirements | Benign calibration only for thresholds; attack-labelled data held out for evaluation only. |
| Chronology availability | No N-BaIoT temporal experiment is specified; exact chronology/split proportions are ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED. |
| Attack assignment/evaluation | Valid per-client attack evaluation is assumed by the NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES experiment contract and required controls. |
| Preprocessing protocol | FEDERATED_CLIENT_LOCAL_STANDARD is confirmatory. FEDERATED_POOLED_MIN_MAX is supportive only. CENTRALIZED_POOLED_MIN_MAX for centralized reference. |
| Split protocol | Fixed, predefined, disjoint train/calibration/test semantics are required; exact non-temporal proportions/rounding are ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED. |
| Calibration support | Benign-only; canonical eligibility n_k_source >= 100; calibration-size ablation may subsample declared sizes. |
| Metrics available/unavailable | FPR; CV(FPR); IQR/range/worst FPR; TPR/recall; balanced accuracy; Macro-F1; P10 Macro-F1; worst BA; AUROC control; mechanism/threshold-estimation metrics. |
| Threshold methods | CENTRALIZED_REFERENCE; SHARED_THRESHOLD; LOCAL_THRESHOLD; FAMILY_THRESHOLD; CLUSTER_THRESHOLD; pooled/sample-weighted shared controls; shrinkage; size-aware shrinkage; local conformal; benign federated summary statistics; optional variants. |
| Family-taxonomy availability | Defensible physical-device family taxonomy exists and may support FAMILY_THRESHOLD; exact mapping ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED. |
| Temporal eligibility | Not the verified temporal population. |
| Row conservation/leakage/provenance | Same predefined partitions across compared threshold policies; all nine clients visible in mechanism reporting. |
| Permitted claims | May support sole confirmatory shared-versus-local operating-point equity claim on natural devices; may support mechanism/supportive/stress-test claims by declared tier. |
| Forbidden claims/limitations | No fleet-scale validation; no universal threshold superiority; no general drift/privacy/deployment claims. |
| Roadmap source | L605–617, L1497–1519, L1716–1821 |

### DATASET-CICIOT2023 — CICIoT2023
| Field | Roadmap-derived contract |
| --- | --- |
| Scientific role | Dataset-specific applicability boundary only for the available processed artifact. |
| Available data semantics | Original publication describes 105 devices and 33 attacks grouped into seven categories, but available artifact lacks verified physical-device mapping. |
| Client identity / permissible populations | CICIOT_FILE_CLIENTS: 63 file-defined pseudo-clients. Original 105-device topology must not be reconstructed from missing metadata. |
| Forbidden population constructions | No physical-device repartitioning; no artificial device grouping as substitute; no inferred chronology; no device-aware wording; no generalization of null result to original 105-device topology. |
| Feature requirements | Model input gate requires normalized label recognized AND every declared model-input feature finite. Canonical raw-fidelity rows remain lossless. |
| Label requirements | Gate independently records missing/unrecognized label and non-finite feature signals; never infer labels. |
| Chronology availability | Valid timestamps absent/insufficient for temporal probing; pseudo-time forbidden. |
| Attack assignment/evaluation | Roadmap does not authorize device-aware attack claims. Attack-sensitive pseudo-client evaluation beyond listed permitted analyses is ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED/NOT_APPLICABLE to the boundary programme. |
| Preprocessing protocol | No imputation, zero-fill, caps, clipping, infinity replacement, or label inference; ineligible rows excluded before construction/split/fit/calibration/evaluation. |
| Split protocol | File-defined client construction after eligibility gate; exact split proportions/rounding ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED. |
| Calibration support | Benign-only threshold calibration; canonical eligibility applies. |
| Metrics available/unavailable | Pairwise benign JS divergence; CV(FPR); IQR; range; worst pseudo-client FPR; descriptive quantile-estimation comparisons. |
| Threshold methods | CENTRALIZED_REFERENCE; SHARED_THRESHOLD; LOCAL_THRESHOLD; CLUSTER_THRESHOLD if meaningful; FAMILY_THRESHOLD unavailable. |
| Family-taxonomy availability | Unavailable; no defensible physical-device family taxonomy for file pseudo-clients. |
| Temporal eligibility | Suppressed; inferred chronology invalid. |
| Row conservation/leakage/provenance | Stable row identity/source provenance must be preserved; eligibility gate identical across methods. |
| Permitted claims | Only file-defined pseudo-client applicability-boundary statements. |
| Forbidden claims/limitations | No device-level generalization; physical-client equity; temporal behavior; original-topology device-aware threshold performance. |
| Roadmap source | L619–634, L1521–1556, L2460–2480 |

### DATASET-EDGEIIOTSET — Edge-IIoTset
| Field | Roadmap-derived contract |
| --- | --- |
| Scientific role | Sole new external dataset for benign operating-point equity; also sole verified temporal boundary dataset. |
| Available data semantics | Independent IoT/IIoT testbed. Static benign population has ten sensor-group folders; temporal population has nine groups because Modbus timestamps are unusable. |
| Client identity / permissible populations | EDGE_SENSOR_GROUPS: 10 static benign sensor-group clients including Modbus. EDGE_TEMPORAL_GROUPS: 9 verified temporal groups excluding Modbus. |
| Forbidden population constructions | No fabricated per-client attack assignment; no inherited attack metrics; no FAMILY_THRESHOLD without taxonomy; no extra external dataset; no pseudo-time. |
| Feature requirements | Canonical lexical provenance retained. Immutable 33-column numeric projection from 11,209,913 static benign rows; exact ordered list locked. Strict finite numeric parsing only. |
| Label requirements | Outcome/provenance fields do not enter model input. Attack traffic confined to attacker's subnet prevents valid per-client attack assignment. |
| Chronology availability | Verified genuine capture time for nine temporal groups; Modbus frame.time values are address literals and exclude it from temporal population. |
| Attack assignment/evaluation | Per-client TPR/recall/Macro-F1/P10/BA/worst BA/AUROC/attack-sensitive trade-offs unavailable by design for external client population. |
| Preprocessing protocol | 33-column projection; no fill/coercion/hash/ordinal/one-hot/vocabulary fitting for mixed lexical fields. General named preprocessing state still fixed; exact selected normalization identity for EDGE_SENSOR_GROUPS is not separately restated. |
| Split protocol | Static exact proportions ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED. Temporal split 55% train / 15% historical calibration / 10% future recalibration / 20% future evaluation. Matched static reference uses same row budget with 10% reserve. |
| Calibration support | Benign-only; static eligible-benign coverage 1.0 under n_k_source >= 100; future recalibration benign and precedes future evaluation. |
| Metrics available/unavailable | Per-client benign FPR; CV(FPR); IQR/range/worst FPR; threshold dispersion; benign score-distribution analysis; temporal drift/recovery quantities. Attack-sensitive metrics unavailable. |
| Threshold methods | SHARED_THRESHOLD; LOCAL_THRESHOLD; CLUSTER_THRESHOLD; benign federated summary comparator; quantile sensitivity; calibration-size/shrinkage where supported; FAMILY_THRESHOLD omitted. |
| Family-taxonomy availability | No defensible family taxonomy established for ten sensor groups. |
| Temporal eligibility | Eligible only for verified nine-group temporal experiment with genuine timestamps. |
| Row conservation/leakage/provenance | Null/non-finite retained numeric fields excluded with explicit provenance; feature order fixed; chronological stable sort preserves duplicate timestamp row order. |
| Permitted claims | Independent external benign-equity validation; bounded one-shot threshold-aging/recalibration evidence. |
| Forbidden claims/limitations | No external cross-client attack-detection equity; no concept-drift solution; no streaming/online/drift-triggered adaptation; no deployment-readiness. |
| Roadmap source | L644–677, L1595–1710, L2397–2458, L2617–2714 |

## 12. Score-generation contract

| Contract field | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Scorer input | Selected frozen detector state plus the exact fitted preprocessing state and declared split rows. |
| Preprocessing state | Same named fitted state across core threshold policies; stress-test models use their own compatible detector/scoring artifacts. |
| Detector state | Core: one frozen FedAvg detector per seed/population. CENTRALIZED_REFERENCE, FedProx, and Ditto use separate states. |
| Client identity | Every score remains tied to the declared client/pseudo-client/sensor group and stable row identity. |
| Split identity | Calibration scores originate only from declared calibration rows; test scores from held-out evaluation rows; temporal future states preserve window identity. |
| Score type | Autoencoder reconstruction error; higher error is greater anomaly evidence. |
| Prediction operator | Attack iff `error > threshold`; benign iff `error <= threshold`; operator fixed across policies. |
| Labels alongside scores | Held-out labels stay associated with held-out test scores. Calibration threshold inputs are benign-only. |
| Calibration score reuse | Same base calibration scores across core policies; only declared subsampling/future recalibration changes calibration input. |
| Evaluation score reuse | Same held-out test scores/labels across core policies; separate score sets required when detector changes. |
| Immutability/policy independence | Threshold methods never alter or regenerate scores in the core ladder. |
| Numerical tolerance | RESOLVED (was AMBIG-004). Two distinct notions: `SCIENTIFIC_ARTIFACT_IDENTITY` (policy-level score/AUROC equality is proven by matching score-artifact identity, ordered row identities, client/split/detector/checkpoint/preprocessing identity, and evaluation labels — never by numerical closeness) versus `NUMERICAL_RELOAD_EQUIVALENCE` (the `1e-12` absolute tolerance, applicable only to serialization/reload numerical equivalence). `1e-12` must never be promoted to threshold-policy score/AUROC identity. |
| Persistence | Required by downstream reuse/provenance, but serialization format is ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED. |
| Reload validation | Must preserve score values and row/label identity sufficiently to establish fixed-score comparison. |
| Provenance | Detector, checkpoint, preprocessing, dataset, population, client, split, row, and seed identities must be provable; exact hash mechanism ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED. |

## 13. Calibration contract

| Rule | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Benign-only calibration | Every core threshold and DATP-compatible threshold variant uses benign calibration data only. |
| Eligibility | Canonical primary-analysis eligibility: `n_k_source >= 100` benign calibration samples; decided before test evaluation and identical across compared policies. |
| Client calibration sets | Core policies receive the same client calibration records before any declared subsampling. |
| Pooled/grouped calibration | Shared/family/cluster/comparator constructions may aggregate only the declared benign calibration quantities appropriate to the method. |
| Future recalibration | Only EDGE_TEMPORAL_GROUPS uses the dedicated 10% future benign recalibration window; it must precede future evaluation. |
| Prohibited attack access | Attack-labelled records cannot influence threshold, q, eligibility, checkpoint, comparator tuning, shrinkage, conformal alpha, K/features, or external client construction. |
| Prohibited evaluation access | Held-out evaluation cannot tune calibration/threshold parameters. |
| Support insufficiency | Ineligible clients excluded from primary CV(FPR); experiment-specific fallback only if explicitly declared. |
| Fallback behavior | Silent fallback forbidden. Deployment fallback is allowed only in an explicit fallback experiment; no such concrete fallback algorithm is locked in this roadmap. |
| Calibration-size experiment | RESOLVED (was AMBIG-002). Experimental sample size `m` in {50,100,250,500,1000,5000}, distinct from canonical eligibility `n_k_source >= 100`; 10 deterministic without-replacement nested replicates per training seed/client/size; `(client, m)` feasible iff `n_k_source >= m`; `m = 50` is a resolved sample-starved supportive/diagnostic condition, never a canonical-eligibility redefinition; cross-size comparisons use the feasible-client intersection. |
| Conformal calibration | Benign local nonconformity scores only; alpha=0.05 main diagnostic; held-out benign coverage used for evaluation. |
| Comparator calibration | FEDERATED_BENIGN_SUMMARY_STATISTICS_THRESHOLD communicates only benign summary statistics and must match target exceedance `1-q`. |

## 18. Anchor reproduction and verification

**RESOLVED (was AMBIG-005).** The vague "not materially inconsistent" gate is replaced by one explicit, deterministic anchor reproduction/compatibility gate. This is an anchor reproduction/compatibility gate; it is **not** a formal statistical equivalence test, and no additional equivalence margin is invented.

### Anchor reproduction
- Preserve the `anchor` as the conference-faithful reference protocol identity.
- Reproduce the locked **five-seed subset** with the journal implementation before extending the confirmatory procedure to ten seeds.
- Preserve historical anchor endpoint/checkpoint semantics; do not retrofit the journal fixed-round-200 rule simply to improve reproduction.
- The historical N-BaIoT confirmatory preprocessing is per-client `StandardScaler` fitted on benign train only, as stated by the roadmap rationale.
- Exact anchor architecture/training hyperparameters/checkpoint candidate set are not restated here: `ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED` in this roadmap.

### Anchor verification — locked historical reference and acceptance conditions

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Reference 95% BCa interval | `[0.647, 0.769]` (NUM-0110) |
| Reference interval width | `0.122` (NUM-0111) |
| Maximum width multiplier | `1.20` (NUM-0112) |
| Maximum exact reproduced interval width | `0.1464` = `1.20 x 0.122` (NUM-0113; FORMULA-072) — the **operative exact bound** |
| Display-only rounded value | `0.147` (NUM-0114) — display only, never a second looser threshold |

The reproduced five-seed anchor passes only when **all fourteen** conditions hold:

1. the exact historical five-seed cohort is used;
2. the historical anchor dataset identity is preserved;
3. the historical client population is preserved;
4. the historical preprocessing identity is preserved;
5. the historical training protocol is preserved;
6. the historical checkpoint-selection semantics are preserved;
7. the historical scoring semantics are preserved;
8. the historical threshold semantics are preserved;
9. the historical eligibility semantics are preserved;
10. the historical metric definition is preserved;
11. the reproduced 95% BCa interval remains entirely positive;
12. the reproduced interval overlaps `[0.647, 0.769]`;
13. the reproduced interval width is `<= 0.1464`;
14. required artifact lineage, provenance, identity, serialization, and reload-validation gates pass.

If every condition passes, the existing appropriate anchor-success state is emitted and execution may proceed to the ten-seed extension. If the ten-seed result is weaker or materially different, the ten-seed evidence still becomes the main result and the five-seed result is labelled preliminary — this labeling occurs only after gate success, never as a substitute for it.

### Anchor status — `ANCHOR_REPRODUCTION_FAILED`

If **any** of the fourteen conditions fails, the anchor status is exactly `ANCHOR_REPRODUCTION_FAILED`. This status:

- blocks the ten-seed journal extension;
- blocks downstream journal claim-generating execution;
- requires investigation;
- requires a successful anchor reproduction before proceeding;
- is not overridden by supportive evidence, external validation, or favorable alternative threshold methods;
- is never relaxed after observing the result — the fourteen conditions above cannot be loosened post hoc.

### Anchor acceptance gate — deterministic path

```text
ANCHOR_REPRODUCTION -> ANCHOR_VERIFICATION -> ANCHOR_ACCEPTANCE_GATE -> JOURNAL_EXECUTION_ALLOWED / JOURNAL_EXECUTION_BLOCKED
```

There is exactly one deterministic path: anchor reproduction → anchor verification → anchor acceptance verdict → permission (`JOURNAL_EXECUTION_ALLOWED`, ten-seed extension proceeds) or prohibition (`JOURNAL_EXECUTION_BLOCKED` / `ANCHOR_REPRODUCTION_FAILED`) to continue. No undefined failure path remains.

### What may proceed only after anchor success
- The ten-seed extension and all downstream journal claim-generating execution proceed **only** after `ANCHOR_ACCEPTANCE_GATE` emits its success verdict.
- A failed gate (`ANCHOR_REPRODUCTION_FAILED`) formally blocks all later execution; this is no longer `ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED` (previously logged as `AMBIG-005`, now resolved).

#### Lossless normalized roadmap contract

**5.1 NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES shared-versus-local threshold-scope confirmation**

**Scientific role**

**Confirmatory.** This is the only experiment that can establish the locked main journal endpoint.

**Question**

Under one fixed FedAvg autoencoder per seed, does changing the calibration scope from one shared threshold (SHARED_THRESHOLD) to one threshold per physical device (LOCAL_THRESHOLD) reduce cross-client false-positive-rate dispersion on N-BaIoT?

**Why the experiment is necessary**

The conference result used five seeds. The journal extension must reproduce that evidence and expand it to ten paired seeds without suppressing a less favorable estimate.

**Population and inputs**

- NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES;
- nine physical-device clients;
- ten paired training seeds;
- one locked primary checkpoint per seed;
- benign calibration scores;
- held-out benign and attack test scores;
- unchanged eligibility.

**Fixed elements**

- autoencoder architecture;
- FedAvg training;
- local epochs `E = 1`;
- full participation;
- preprocessing;
- checkpoint-selection rule;
- quantile `q = 0.95`;
- test records;
- metric implementation.

**Experimental factor**

Threshold-calibration scope:

- SHARED_THRESHOLD shared threshold;
- LOCAL_THRESHOLD per-client threshold.

**Procedure**

1. Reproduce the locked five-seed subset using the journal implementation.
2. Apply the anchor reproduction gate (§5.2; §18 of the Audit Matrix) to the reproduced five-seed result. Do not proceed to step 3 unless the gate emits an anchor-success verdict; otherwise the status is `ANCHOR_REPRODUCTION_FAILED` and execution is blocked.
3. Extend execution to ten paired seeds.
4. For every seed, compute per-client FPR under SHARED_THRESHOLD and LOCAL_THRESHOLD.
5. Compute `CV(FPR)` over the same eligible clients.
6. Compute the paired seed-level contrast:

\[
\Delta_s
=
CV(FPR)_{SHARED_THRESHOLD,s}
-
CV(FPR)_{LOCAL_THRESHOLD,s}
\]

7. Report all ten seed-level contrasts.
8. Compute the locked 95% BCa confidence interval over the ten paired contrasts.
9. Report sign consistency.
10. Report IQR and max–min FPR alongside CV to guard against small-denominator distortion.
11. Report detection-quality controls for NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES without treating them as the primary verdict.

**Required outcomes**

- SHARED_THRESHOLD and LOCAL_THRESHOLD per-client FPR for every seed;
- seed-level SHARED_THRESHOLD and LOCAL_THRESHOLD `CV(FPR)`;
- ten paired deltas;
- mean or median paired delta, as defined in the evaluation protocol;
- 95% BCa interval;
- sign-consistency count;
- IQR and range;
- Macro-F1, balanced accuracy, TPR, and P10 Macro-F1 controls;
- complete nine-client result display.

**Statistical unit and analysis**

The training seed is the independent unit.

The BCa interval is the confirmatory inferential result. Wilcoxon signed-rank and matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation are descriptive secondary evidence.

**Interpretation rules**

**Confirmatory support**
The 95% BCa interval excludes zero in the positive direction.

**Directional but inconclusive**
The point estimate is positive, but the interval touches or crosses zero.

**No observed advantage**
The estimate is approximately null and the interval includes zero.

**Opposite direction**
LOCAL_THRESHOLD increases `CV(FPR)` relative to SHARED_THRESHOLD.

**Confirmatory inference unavailable (resolves AMBIG-006)**
The locked 95% BCa interval cannot validly be produced. The confirmatory claim is not established; no other interval or test substitutes for it.

Every outcome becomes the main ten-seed result. The five-seed result is labelled preliminary when the ten-seed evidence is weaker or materially different.

**Prohibited uses**

- no checkpoint selection from this result;
- no replacement by CLUSTER_THRESHOLD, shrinkage, or LOCAL_SPLIT_CONFORMAL_THRESHOLD if the endpoint fails;
- no removal of unfavorable seeds;
- no claim that LOCAL_THRESHOLD improves overall detection performance.

**6.1 Shared-threshold construction sensitivity**

**Scientific role**

**Supportive.**

**Question**

Is the observed SHARED_THRESHOLD-versus-LOCAL_THRESHOLD difference caused specifically by SHARED_THRESHOLD’s arithmetic mean of local quantiles, or does it persist across alternative shared-threshold constructions?

**Comparison set**

- SHARED_THRESHOLD arithmetic mean of local quantiles;
- exact pooled benign quantile;
- sample-weighted shared construction;
- LOCAL_THRESHOLD local quantiles.

**Procedure**

Use the same NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES model, scores, clients, and seeds as the confirmatory experiment. Recompute thresholds only.

For each shared construction:

- compute the shared threshold;
- evaluate all eligible clients;
- compute `CV(FPR)`, IQR, range, and worst-client FPR;
- calculate the paired difference relative to LOCAL_THRESHOLD;
- report achieved pooled and per-client exceedance.

**Interpretation**

**Robust construction effect**
All reasonable shared constructions retain higher FPR dispersion than LOCAL_THRESHOLD.

**Construction-specific effect**
One shared construction approaches or outperforms LOCAL_THRESHOLD. The claim is narrowed to the locked SHARED_THRESHOLD construction.

**No shared-versus-local distinction**
Shared constructions and LOCAL_THRESHOLD are practically similar.

This experiment cannot alter the definition of the confirmatory SHARED_THRESHOLD endpoint.

**6.2 Quantile-level sensitivity**

**Scientific role**

**Supportive threshold sensitivity.**

**Question**

Does the SHARED_THRESHOLD/LOCAL_THRESHOLD/CLUSTER_THRESHOLD ordering depend on choosing `q = 0.95`?

**Quantile grid**

```text
q in {0.90, 0.95, 0.975, 0.99}
```

**Procedure**

For every NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES seed and quantile:

- compute SHARED_THRESHOLD, LOCAL_THRESHOLD, and canonical CLUSTER_THRESHOLD;
- evaluate on unchanged held-out test scores;
- report mean FPR, `CV(FPR)`, IQR, range, worst-client FPR, TPR, and P10 Macro-F1;
- report achieved benign exceedance against the target `1 - q`;
- visualize the policy-by-quantile surface.

Where EDGE_SENSOR_GROUPS supports the same calculation, repeat only the benign-FPR outcomes.

**Interpretation**

An ordering inversion is reported directly. The canonical `q = 0.95` is not changed after inspection.

#### Lossless normalized roadmap contract

**6.3 Controlled non-IID severity**

**Scientific role**

**Supportive heterogeneity analysis.**

**Question**

Does stronger client heterogeneity increase the operating-point advantage of local threshold calibration?

**Population and factors**

- NBAIOT_DIRICHLET_CLIENTS;
- 20 synthetic clients;
- Dirichlet severity grid:
  - `0.1`;
  - `0.3`;
  - `0.5`;
  - `1.0`;
  - `10.0`;
  - IID;
- SHARED_THRESHOLD, LOCAL_THRESHOLD, and CLUSTER_THRESHOLD;
- ten paired seeds where feasible.

**Procedure**

For every seed and severity:

1. construct the partition using the locked seed and partition rule;
2. retain the pre-specified partition;
3. train a separate `FEDAVG` detector for this `(training seed, heterogeneity severity)` cell under the fixed training protocol — this includes IID as one severity condition in this grid; never reuse another severity's fitted preprocessing state, detector weights, checkpoint, calibration scores, or evaluation scores;
4. compute SHARED_THRESHOLD, LOCAL_THRESHOLD, and CLUSTER_THRESHOLD;
5. report heterogeneity diagnostics;
6. compute the SHARED_THRESHOLD–LOCAL_THRESHOLD `CV(FPR)` difference;
7. report uncertainty per alpha;
8. display seed distributions rather than only point estimates.

**Detector training discipline (resolves AMBIG-003)**

For every `(training seed, heterogeneity severity)` cell, including IID, a separate `FEDAVG` detector is trained. The training protocol remains fixed across severities (model family; architecture apart from feature-schema input dimension; optimizer; loss; hyperparameters; local epoch count; participation; aggregation semantics; round budget; checkpoint candidates/selection rule; training-seed semantics; named preprocessing protocol identity), but population-dependent fitted preprocessing state, detector weights, checkpoint, calibration scores, and evaluation scores must never be reused across different severity cells. Within one fixed `(seed, severity)` cell, SHARED_THRESHOLD, LOCAL_THRESHOLD, and CLUSTER_THRESHOLD reuse exactly the same frozen detector, checkpoint, fitted preprocessing state, calibration scores, evaluation scores, evaluation labels, and eligibility state.

**Required heterogeneity diagnostics**

At minimum:

- client sample-count distribution;
- client benign-distribution divergence;
- class or attack composition when valid;
- eligible-client coverage;
- pairwise or aggregate Jensen–Shannon divergence.

**Interpretation**

A smooth monotone curve is not required. Low-alpha conditions may form one broad high-heterogeneity band. The result is associative and does not establish that the selected heterogeneity statistic causally determines DATP benefit.

Comparisons across heterogeneity severities are `SUPPORTIVE_ASSOCIATIVE`, not threshold-only causal comparisons. Changing heterogeneity changes the federated training problem and may change the resulting detector; cross-severity results must not be interpreted as isolating a causal effect of heterogeneity on threshold scope independently of detector learning.

#### Lossless normalized roadmap contract

**7.1 Threshold-sharing granularity and cluster stability**

**Scientific role**

**Mechanism analysis.**

**Questions**

- Does family or cluster threshold sharing recover part of LOCAL_THRESHOLD’s FPR-equity benefit?
- How much calibration granularity is required?
- Are CLUSTER_THRESHOLD client assignments stable across seeds and calibration samples?
- Does cluster sharing provide a defensible middle ground between one global threshold and one threshold per client?

**Population**

- NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES is mandatory;
- EDGE_SENSOR_GROUPS may include CLUSTER_THRESHOLD;
- FAMILY_THRESHOLD remains NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES only.

**Comparison set**

- SHARED_THRESHOLD shared;
- FAMILY_THRESHOLD family;
- CLUSTER_THRESHOLD canonical `K = 3`;
- LOCAL_THRESHOLD local;
- exploratory CLUSTER_THRESHOLD cluster counts where mathematically feasible.

**Procedure**

1. Build each client fingerprint from benign calibration errors only.
2. Standardize fingerprint dimensions using the locked rule.
3. Fit canonical k-means with locked initialization and seed handling.
4. Assign the cluster-level threshold.
5. Evaluate FPR equity and detection controls.
6. Repeat clustering across seeds and declared resamples.
7. compare assignments using adjusted Rand index.
8. compute within-cluster and across-cluster threshold and FPR dispersion.
9. display the client-to-cluster membership for every seed.
10. compare CLUSTER_THRESHOLD groupings against the device-family taxonomy descriptively without treating taxonomy agreement as the optimization target.

Adjusted Rand index is appropriate as a chance-adjusted comparison of two partitions, but the very small NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES client count requires displaying the underlying assignments and contingency tables rather than relying on ARI alone.[^ari]

**Required outcomes**

- SHARED_THRESHOLD/FAMILY_THRESHOLD/CLUSTER_THRESHOLD/LOCAL_THRESHOLD `CV(FPR)`;
- worst-client FPR;
- IQR and range;
- CLUSTER_THRESHOLD recovery fraction relative to the SHARED_THRESHOLD–LOCAL_THRESHOLD gap;
- within-cluster and across-cluster dispersion;
- ARI across seed pairs or declared resamples;
- complete membership assignments;
- cluster sizes;
- empty or singleton cluster diagnostics;
- detection-quality controls for NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES.

**Interpretation**

**Useful middle ground**
CLUSTER_THRESHOLD or FAMILY_THRESHOLD recovers a meaningful portion of LOCAL_THRESHOLD’s equity improvement with stable groupings.

**Performance without stability**
CLUSTER_THRESHOLD reduces dispersion, but assignments are unstable. The result is reported as fragile.

**Stable but unhelpful**
Clusters repeat, but do not improve the operating point.

**No cluster mechanism**
CLUSTER_THRESHOLD is unstable and provides little recovery. CLUSTER_THRESHOLD remains an explored negative mechanism result.

**7.4 Heterogeneity–benefit association**

**Scientific role**

**Mechanism association.**

**Question**

Does benign score-distribution heterogeneity predict the magnitude of the local-threshold benefit?

**Procedure**

For each valid regime/seed unit:

- calculate the locked Jensen–Shannon heterogeneity summary from benign score distributions;
- calculate the SHARED_THRESHOLD–LOCAL_THRESHOLD FPR-equity gain;
- plot both;
- report Spearman correlation;
- fit the pre-specified descriptive regression;
- report `R²`, uncertainty, leverage, and sensitivity to individual clients or regimes.

**Interpretation**

A strong relationship supports a heterogeneity-conditioned interpretation. A weak relationship is a real result and prevents using JS divergence as a sufficient predictor.

The analysis is associative, not causal.

#### Lossless normalized roadmap contract

**7.5 Threshold movement versus operating-point harm**

**Scientific role**

**Mechanism analysis.**

**Question**

How does the client-specific threshold shift from SHARED_THRESHOLD to LOCAL_THRESHOLD relate to changes in false positives and attack detection?

**Procedure**

For every NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES device and seed, compute:

\[
\Delta \tau_k = \tau_{LOCAL_THRESHOLD,k} - \tau_{SHARED_THRESHOLD}
\]

\[
\Delta FPR_k = FPR_{LOCAL_THRESHOLD,k} - FPR_{SHARED_THRESHOLD,k}
\]

\[
\Delta TPR_k = TPR_{LOCAL_THRESHOLD,k} - TPR_{SHARED_THRESHOLD,k}
\]

Display:

- threshold shift versus FPR change;
- threshold shift versus TPR change;
- device labels;
- seed uncertainty;
- all nine clients without filtering.

**Interpretation**

This experiment quantifies the equity–sensitivity trade-off surface. It does not claim that threshold movement alone explains every detection change.

#### Lossless normalized roadmap contract

**8.1 Calibration-size ablation**

**Scientific role**

**Boundary condition and threshold-variant support.**

**Question**

How much benign calibration data is required before local thresholds become stable?

**Two distinct calibration-size quantities**

`n_k_source` is client `k`'s benign calibration support before any experimental subsampling (canonical eligibility `n_k_source >= 100`). `m` is the calibration sample size drawn for this ablation. Canonical eligibility is fixed from `n_k_source` before this experiment subsamples anything and is never recomputed from `m`.

**Calibration-size grid**

```text
m in {50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 5000}
```

**Feasibility rule**

A `(client, m)` experimental cell is feasible only when `n_k_source >= m`. The `m = 50` condition is an explicit sample-starved supportive/diagnostic condition, deliberately below the canonical deployment-support requirement of `n_k_source >= 100`; it does not redefine canonical eligibility to 50 and does not enter the sole confirmatory endpoint.

**Fixed-cohort comparator discipline**

Within one `m` condition, every compared threshold policy receives the same client cohort and the same source calibration records, deterministic subsampling is policy-independent, and eligibility/feasibility cannot vary by threshold policy. Cross-size population-level comparisons use the intersection of clients feasible across every size directly compared; size-specific cohorts may additionally be reported descriptively only when their coverage and client count are explicit.

**Repetition**

Each subsample size must use multiple deterministic subsampling replicates nested within each training seed. Subsampling replicates quantify calibration sampling variability; they are not counted as independent training seeds.

**Locked replicate count (`CALIBRATION_SUBSAMPLE_REPLICATE_COUNT`, prospective research amendment).** Each subsample size uses `10` deterministic nested replicates per (training seed, client). Ten replicates are enough to summarize within-seed threshold/CV variability at each declared calibration size while keeping the grid computationally bounded; replicates are drawn without replacement via a deterministic hash of `(training_seed, client, replicate_index)` and are always summarized within seed before any across-seed inference (§12.5) — they are never treated as an independent inferential unit and never increase the seed count.

**Comparison set**

- SHARED_THRESHOLD;
- LOCAL_THRESHOLD;
- CLUSTER_THRESHOLD;
- shrinkage overlay where defined;
- LOCAL_SPLIT_CONFORMAL_THRESHOLD where its finite-sample rule is valid.

**Procedure**

For every seed, client, size `m`, and subsample replicate:

1. verify `(client, m)` feasibility (`n_k_source >= m`);
2. draw `m` benign calibration records without replacement from that client's source pool;
3. compute the declared thresholds;
4. evaluate on the unchanged held-out test set;
5. record threshold variance across subsamples;
6. record FPR target error;
7. record `CV(FPR)`, worst-client FPR, IQR, range, P10 Macro-F1, and balanced accuracy over the fixed-cohort intersection defined above for cross-size comparisons;
8. report clients infeasible at each size, with the reason.

**Interpretation**

**Graceful degradation**
LOCAL_THRESHOLD remains stable as calibration shrinks.

**Shrinkage benefit**
Naive LOCAL_THRESHOLD destabilizes while shrinkage reduces variance without erasing most personalization.

**Sample-starved boundary**
Local thresholds become unreliable below a clear range. The `m = 50` cell is always this sample-starved supportive/diagnostic condition, never a canonical eligibility redefinition.

**No sample-size effect**
Threshold stability changes little over the tested grid.

The result cannot be summarized using only the best-performing calibration size.

**8.2 Fixed local–global shrinkage**

**Scientific role**

**Supportive threshold variant.**

**Question**

Can partial pooling retain FPR equity while reducing local-threshold variance or detection loss?

**Factor**

```text
lambda in {0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00}
```

**Procedure**

Using the same NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES scores:

- compute the shrinkage threshold for every eligible client;
- evaluate the full lambda curve;
- report `CV(FPR)`, worst-client FPR, IQR, range, TPR, P10 Macro-F1, and threshold variance;
- repeat within the calibration-size grid where planned;
- do not choose one lambda from the test set and present it as the method.

**Interpretation**

The full curve is the result.

A non-monotone response is reported. An intermediate lambda may be described as a useful empirical compromise only if its selection rule is explicitly exploratory or determined without test leakage.

**8.3 Calibration-size-aware shrinkage**

**Scientific role**

**Supportive extension of shrinkage.**

**Question**

Can personalization weight depend on available benign calibration size without using test outcomes?

**Requirements**

The function `lambda(n_k)` must be:

- specified before evaluation;
- monotone unless a scientific reason justifies otherwise;
- bounded in `[0, 1]`;
- identical across clients apart from `n_k`;
- compared with fixed-lambda curves;
- evaluated over the same calibration-size subsamples.

**Interpretation**

This is an engineering threshold variant, not a new statistical estimator claim.

#### Lossless normalized roadmap contract

**8.4 Split-conformal LOCAL_SPLIT_CONFORMAL_THRESHOLD diagnostic**

**Scientific role**

**Supportive response to the “equalized by construction” critique.**

**Question**

Does a finite-sample-adjusted local conformal quantile achieve the intended benign coverage on held-out data, and does cross-client FPR dispersion remain lower than under a shared threshold?

**Procedure**

For every eligible NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES client and seed:

1. use only the declared benign calibration scores;
2. compute the finite-sample conformal quantile at `alpha = 0.05`;
3. evaluate benign coverage on held-out benign scores;
4. report coverage error per client and seed;
5. evaluate attack-sensitive metrics only on held-out attack scores;
6. compare LOCAL_SPLIT_CONFORMAL_THRESHOLD with LOCAL_THRESHOLD and SHARED_THRESHOLD;
7. report results at small calibration sizes where rank granularity is material.

**Required outcomes**

- target coverage;
- achieved marginal benign coverage;
- coverage error;
- per-client coverage distribution;
- `CV(FPR)`;
- threshold difference from LOCAL_THRESHOLD;
- detection-quality controls;
- finite-sample discreteness diagnostics.

**Interpretation**

LOCAL_SPLIT_CONFORMAL_THRESHOLD can show that the threshold rule is evaluated through held-out coverage rather than assumed to equalize test FPR by construction.

It does not prove client-conditional validity under arbitrary non-IID shift. Exchangeability limitations must remain explicit.[^split-conformal][^fed-conformal-heterogeneity]

**9.1 Benign summary-statistics comparator**

**Scientific role**

**Mandatory comparator stress test.**

**Question**

Does a matched benign-only federated summary-statistics threshold dominate, match, or underperform DATP’s shared and local threshold scopes?

**Population**

- NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES is mandatory;
- EDGE_SENSOR_GROUPS is mandatory for benign-FPR outcomes when artifacts are available.

**Comparison set**

- SHARED_THRESHOLD;
- exact pooled benign quantile;
- sample-weighted shared construction;
- LOCAL_THRESHOLD;
- `FEDERATED_BENIGN_SUMMARY_STATISTICS_THRESHOLD`.

**Matching rule**

The comparator’s target exceedance must be matched to:

```text
1 - q
```

It may not be tuned on attack labels or F1.

**Procedure**

1. compute the exact centralized benign reference;
2. compute every distributed construction from the same calibration records;
3. evaluate threshold-estimation error against the centralized reference;
4. evaluate achieved benign exceedance;
5. evaluate cross-client FPR dispersion;
6. report communication payload estimates separately from measured network cost;
7. calculate the locked between-ratio diagnostic where defined;
8. describe precisely which statistics leave each client.

**Required outcomes**

- threshold value;
- absolute and relative threshold error;
- target-attainment error;
- `CV(FPR)`, IQR, range, and worst-client FPR;
- communication fields and estimated bytes;
- client coverage;
- comparison with SHARED_THRESHOLD and LOCAL_THRESHOLD.

**Interpretation**

`FEDERATED_BENIGN_SUMMARY_STATISTICS_THRESHOLD` may:

- improve over SHARED_THRESHOLD but remain weaker than LOCAL_THRESHOLD;
- match LOCAL_THRESHOLD;
- dominate LOCAL_THRESHOLD;
- fail to improve over SHARED_THRESHOLD.

Every outcome is reported. The result does not support a faithful Laridi claim because anomalous validation summaries are excluded.[^laridi]

#### Lossless normalized roadmap contract

**10.1 Edge-IIoTset external benign-equity validation**

**Scientific role**

**External validation.**

**Question**

Does the shared-versus-local threshold-scope effect appear on an independent sensor-group-partitioned IoT/IIoT dataset?

**Population**

- EDGE_SENSOR_GROUPS;
- ten benign sensor-group clients;
- eligible-benign coverage 1.0;
- ten paired seeds where training is feasible.

**Comparison set**

- SHARED_THRESHOLD;
- LOCAL_THRESHOLD;
- CLUSTER_THRESHOLD canonical;
- `FEDERATED_BENIGN_SUMMARY_STATISTICS_THRESHOLD`;
- quantile sensitivity;
- calibration-size and shrinkage analyses where supported.

FAMILY_THRESHOLD is omitted.

**Procedure**

1. train the FedAvg autoencoder per seed using benign training data;
2. construct the allowed thresholds;
3. evaluate per-client benign FPR;
4. compute cross-client equity metrics;
5. represent attack-sensitive per-client metrics as unavailable;
6. compare the direction and magnitude of SHARED_THRESHOLD–LOCAL_THRESHOLD with NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES without treating the datasets as exchangeable replications.

**Required outcomes**

- eligible-benign coverage;
- per-client benign sample counts;
- SHARED_THRESHOLD/LOCAL_THRESHOLD/CLUSTER_THRESHOLD/`FEDERATED_BENIGN_SUMMARY_STATISTICS_THRESHOLD` thresholds;
- per-client FPR;
- `CV(FPR)`, IQR, range, and worst-client FPR;
- seed-level SHARED_THRESHOLD–LOCAL_THRESHOLD differences;
- BCa interval as external evidence;
- typed unavailability for attack-sensitive metrics;
- dataset-specific limitations.

**Interpretation**

**Consistent direction**
Supports external benign-equity validation.

**Weaker or null effect**
Defines a cross-dataset boundary.

**Opposite effect**
Narrows the generalization claim.

**Client assignment or eligibility failure**
Produces an infeasibility result; it cannot be repaired by inventing another partition after inspection.

**10.2 CICIoT2023 file-level boundary**

**Scientific role**

**Applicability boundary.**

**Question**

When the processed client partitions are near-homogeneous and file-defined, is threshold personalization unnecessary or unidentifiable?

**Procedure**

- quantify pairwise benign-distribution divergence;
- run SHARED_THRESHOLD and LOCAL_THRESHOLD on the same scores;
- include CLUSTER_THRESHOLD only if cluster sizes are meaningful;
- report `CV(FPR)`, IQR, range, and worst pseudo-client FPR;
- keep all wording specific to the available pseudo-clients.

**Interpretation**

A null result is not evidence that DATP fails on CICIoT2023’s original physical devices. It is evidence that the available file-defined pseudo-clients do not expose a strong threshold-scope need.

#### Lossless normalized roadmap contract

**11.1 FedProx aggregation stress test**

**Scientific role**

**External aggregation-side stress test.**

**Question**

Does heterogeneity-aware training absorb the SHARED_THRESHOLD–LOCAL_THRESHOLD threshold-scope effect?

**Literature rationale**

FedProx was designed to address systems and statistical heterogeneity by adding a proximal term to local optimization and generalizing FedAvg.[^fedprox] Its inclusion tests whether better training alignment removes the need for post-training threshold personalization.

**Population**

- NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES is mandatory;
- EDGE_SENSOR_GROUPS benign-equity outcomes are included after EDGE_SENSOR_GROUPS readiness.

**Factors**

- FedAvg reference;
- FedProx with frozen `mu` grid:
  - `0.001`;
  - `0.01`;
  - `0.1`;
  - `1.0`;
- SHARED_THRESHOLD, LOCAL_THRESHOLD, FAMILY_THRESHOLD where valid, and CLUSTER_THRESHOLD.

**Coefficient-selection rule**

The primary FedProx coefficient must be selected using the pre-registered, non-test rule on NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES. The test set, attack labels, `CV(FPR)` advantage, and EDGE_SENSOR_GROUPS outcomes cannot choose `mu`.

**Locked non-test rule (`FEDPROX_MINIMUM_TERMINAL_TRAINING_LOSS`, prospective research amendment).** Among the frozen coefficient grid, the primary FedProx coefficient is the value of `mu` whose population-weighted aggregate federated training loss at the fixed terminal checkpoint round (`200`, the same round `FIXED_TERMINAL_MAXIMUM_ROUND` locks for checkpoint selection) is lowest, averaged across the confirmatory seed cohort on NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES. Ties are broken by selecting the smallest candidate `mu`. This rule uses only benign federated training-loss trajectories already produced during FedProx training; it never inspects held-out test data, attack labels, `CV(FPR)`, threshold outcomes, or EDGE_SENSOR_GROUPS results. The rule mirrors the original FedProx proposal's own training-loss-driven coefficient behavior and standard benchmark practice of tuning `mu` against training-time convergence signals rather than held-out task performance.[^fedprox]

The complete grid remains reportable regardless of which coefficient is selected as primary.

**Procedure**

1. train FedProx models independently from FedAvg;
2. apply the same checkpoint protocol;
3. produce separate score sets;
4. evaluate the complete threshold ladder on each trained model;
5. calculate the SHARED_THRESHOLD–LOCAL_THRESHOLD threshold-scope difference under FedAvg and FedProx;
6. compare convergence and model-quality controls;
7. report training failure or instability without changing the grid retroactively.

**Interpretation**

- retained threshold-scope effect;
- partial absorption;
- full absorption;
- opposite effect;
- FedProx non-convergence or instability.

FedProx results do not enter the core causal ladder.

#### Lossless normalized roadmap contract

**11.2 Ditto model-personalization stress test**

**Scientific role**

**External model-side personalization stress test.**

**Question**

Does maintaining a personalized model for each client make threshold personalization redundant?

**Literature rationale**

Ditto jointly maintains global and personalized models and was proposed as a general personalized federated-learning framework for statistically heterogeneous clients.[^ditto] It is used here because it can be applied without requiring a hand-defined shared representation/local head split.

**Population**

- NBAIOT_NATURAL_DEVICES is mandatory;
- EDGE_SENSOR_GROUPS is included for benign-equity outcomes after readiness.

**Primary comparison**

The interpretable 2-by-2 core is:

- FedAvg model with SHARED_THRESHOLD;
- FedAvg model with LOCAL_THRESHOLD;
- Ditto personalized model with SHARED_THRESHOLD;
- Ditto personalized model with LOCAL_THRESHOLD.

FAMILY_THRESHOLD and CLUSTER_THRESHOLD may be applied as supplementary threshold scopes to the personalized scores.

**Procedure**

1. train genuine Ditto global and personalized states;
2. keep personalized states separate by client;
3. select personalization hyperparameters without attack-test or confirmatory leakage;
4. generate scores separately from the FedAvg artifacts;
5. compute SHARED_THRESHOLD and LOCAL_THRESHOLD on the Ditto score distributions;
6. calculate the threshold-scope gain under FedAvg and under Ditto;
7. report model-quality, FPR-equity, compute, storage, and communication differences;
8. preserve all four core corners.

**Absorption measure**

\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{FedAvg}}
=
CV(FPR)_{\mathrm{FedAvg+SHARED_THRESHOLD}}
-
CV(FPR)_{\mathrm{FedAvg+LOCAL_THRESHOLD}}
\]

\[
\Delta_{\mathrm{Ditto}}
=
CV(FPR)_{\mathrm{Ditto+SHARED_THRESHOLD}}
-
CV(FPR)_{\mathrm{Ditto+LOCAL_THRESHOLD}}
\]

Interpretation bands:

- `Delta_Ditto >= 0.75 * Delta_FedAvg`: threshold personalization remains strongly useful;
- `0.25 * Delta_FedAvg <= Delta_Ditto < 0.75 * Delta_FedAvg`: partial absorption;
- `Delta_Ditto < 0.25 * Delta_FedAvg`: largely absorbed;
- if `CV(FPR)[Ditto+SHARED_THRESHOLD]` is within `0.05` of `CV(FPR)[FedAvg+LOCAL_THRESHOLD]`, model personalization is reported as an alternative route to operating-point equity.

**Scope boundary**

This is one stress test, not an exhaustive personalized-FL benchmark. APFL, Per-FedAvg, pFedMe, FedRep, FedPer, and broad architecture comparisons are not added to this paper.

#### Lossless normalized roadmap contract

**12.1 One-shot recalibration under genuine chronology**

**Scientific role**

**Temporal boundary condition.**

**Question**

When thresholds are calibrated on historical benign behavior, does future benign behavior increase cross-client FPR dispersion, and can one future benign recalibration window recover it?

**Population**

- EDGE_TEMPORAL_GROUPS;
- nine verified temporal groups;
- Modbus excluded;
- ten paired seeds where feasible.

**Compared states**

**Static reference**
Random-fractional split over the same nine groups, used to estimate ordinary sampling variation without chronology.

**Frozen future**
Thresholds fitted from historical calibration and applied unchanged to future evaluation.

**One-shot recalibrated future**
Thresholds recomputed once from the future recalibration window and applied to future evaluation.

**Policies**

- SHARED_THRESHOLD;
- LOCAL_THRESHOLD;
- CLUSTER_THRESHOLD;
- shrinkage where pre-specified.

**Procedure**

1. verify timestamps for every included client;
2. apply stable chronological ordering;
3. construct the 55/15/10/20 split;
4. fit preprocessing and the autoencoder without future leakage;
5. construct historical thresholds;
6. evaluate frozen thresholds on future evaluation;
7. recompute thresholds from future recalibration only;
8. evaluate recalibrated thresholds on the same future evaluation;
9. construct the matched static reference;
10. calculate:

\[
drift\_excess
=
CV_{\mathrm{frozen\ future}}
-
CV_{\mathrm{static\ reference}}
\]

\[
recovered\_amount
=
CV_{\mathrm{frozen\ future}}
-
CV_{\mathrm{recalibrated\ future}}
\]

\[
recovery\_ratio
=
\frac{recovered\_amount}{drift\_excess}
\]

`recovery_ratio` is undefined when `drift_excess` is not meaningfully positive.

**Required outcomes**

- chronology-validation record;
- included and excluded clients;
- static-reference CV;
- frozen-future CV;
- recalibrated-future CV;
- drift excess;
- recovered amount;
- recovery ratio when defined;
- per-client FPR trajectories;
- threshold movements;
- paired seed uncertainty.

**Pre-specified interpretations**

**Temporal degradation with recovery**
Frozen future dispersion exceeds the static reference and one-shot recalibration recovers a meaningful portion.

**Temporal degradation without recovery**
Drift excess is positive, but one-shot recalibration provides little or negative recovery.

**No detectable temporal degradation**
Frozen future dispersion does not meaningfully exceed the static reference; recovery ratio remains undefined.

No outcome justifies claiming a complete concept-drift solution.

#### Lossless normalized roadmap contract

**13.1 Alert-burden experiment**

**Scientific role**

**Supportive operational interpretation.**

**Question**

What does a difference in FPR mean in approximate alerts per device per day?

**Required external input**

A real measured or appropriately cited benign traffic rate:

```text
benign decisions or flows per device per unit time
```

**Calculation**

For client \(k\):

\[
alerts_{k,\mathrm{day}}
=
FPR_k
\times
benign\_traffic\_rate_{k,\mathrm{day}}
\]

**Requirements**

- report the rate source;
- report whether the rate is measured, dataset-derived, or externally cited;
- propagate rate assumptions separately from model uncertainty;
- show per-device burden, not only a pooled total;
- use SHARED_THRESHOLD and LOCAL_THRESHOLD at minimum;
- label estimates as estimated when no deployment measurement exists.

**Suppression rule**

When no real or cited rate is available, omit the metric. Do not invent a nominal rate merely to populate a table or figure.

**Manuscript table-plan boundary:** beyond the explicitly required cluster-assignment contingency table, the roadmap requires many result displays but does not assign them to named manuscript tables. Those are therefore `ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED`, not invented here.

## 25. Reporting and publication contract

- Confirmatory manuscript-facing evidence is the ten-seed N-BaIoT SHARED_THRESHOLD-versus-LOCAL_THRESHOLD CV(FPR) result with the locked paired 95% BCa decision rule.
- All remaining evidence must retain its declared supportive/mechanism/external/stress-test/boundary/exploratory tier.
- Supportive/external/exploratory results cannot rescue a failed confirmatory endpoint.
- Null, weak, opposite, unstable, and infeasible mandatory outcomes must be reported.
- Negative trade-offs, including lower-tail detection degradation, must remain visible.
- Unavailable metrics must be reported as unavailable with reason; Edge attack-sensitive per-client outcomes cannot be fabricated.
- AUROC is a model-quality control; fixed-score threshold changes cannot be reported as AUROC improvement.
- Pooled global averages cannot hide client-level false-alarm disparity.
- Communication/storage/message-size quantities are estimates unless genuinely measured; they cannot be called deployment validation.
- Alert burden is published only if a defensible traffic rate source exists and must be labeled estimated unless directly measured.
- Temporal evidence is one-shot bounded recalibration, not concept-drift handling.
- CICIoT2023 wording remains explicitly file-pseudo-client-specific.
- Every figure/table/result must be reproducible from validated evidence artifacts and carry experiment/seed/policy/population provenance.
- Calculations use full precision; presentation rounding only: rates/aggregate metrics 3 decimals, CIs/effect sizes 3 decimals, p-values 3 significant digits (`< 0.001` where appropriate), counts integers, thresholds sufficient digits for decision reproduction.
- No checkpoint/policy/parameter may be selected from test outcomes, and no unfavorable seed/client/result may be removed.

### Forbidden Claims Matrix

| Forbidden Claim ID | Forbidden statement | Why forbidden |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-001 | The study establishes which model or federated-learning algorithm is best. | The scientific question is threshold-calibration scope under fixed detector. |
| FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-002 | LOCAL_THRESHOLD improves AUROC. | Threshold changes cannot change score ranking under fixed scores. |
| FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-003 | DATP improves detection performance overall. | Macro-F1/lower-tail metrics may weaken; primary object is FPR dispersion. |
| FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-004 | DATP/threshold personalization improves every client or every metric. | Roadmap explicitly allows trade-offs and negative outcomes. |
| FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-005 | DATP is privacy preserving or provides a formal privacy guarantee. | No formal privacy mechanism/guarantee is implemented. |
| FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-006 | CLUSTER_THRESHOLD is a privacy mechanism. | Explicitly excluded. |
| FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-007 | Estimated message sizes prove deployment feasibility, edge readiness, or light weight. | No hardware/network/energy/latency validation. |
| FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-008 | The study validates fleet-scale behavior above 100 clients. | No such real fleet validation; synthetic/pseudo-clients do not establish it. |
| FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-009 | The study is a complete FL-IDS framework benchmark or broad FL benchmark. | Scope is bounded. |
| FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-010 | The study solves non-IID federated learning. | It studies threshold scope and bounded stress tests. |
| FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-011 | The study establishes state of the art, universal superiority, or a first-of-kind novelty claim. | Independent evidence beyond roadmap would be required. |
| FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-012 | Edge-IIoTset validates per-client attack detection, TPR, Macro-F1, BA, AUROC, or attack-sensitive equity. | Valid per-client attack assignment is unavailable. |

| FORBIDDEN-CLAIM-015 | Generated pseudo-time can stand in for real chronology. | Explicitly prohibited. |

Two additional resolved, non-substitutable outcome statuses apply narrowly and are never used as generic availability labels: `CONFIRMATORY_INFERENCE_UNAVAILABLE` (resolves AMBIG-006; the locked BCa interval cannot validly be produced, so the confirmatory claim is NOT ESTABLISHED) and `ANCHOR_REPRODUCTION_FAILED` (resolves AMBIG-005; any of the fourteen anchor-gate conditions fails, blocking the ten-seed extension and downstream journal claim-generating execution).
