## 29. Global audit checklists

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST A — Scientific identity
- [ ] Confirm the central research question remains threshold-calibration scope on a frozen detector, not model/FL-algorithm superiority.
- [ ] Confirm DATP-Core strengthens the original study along exactly six bounded directions (resolves AMBIG-001); evidence tiers and experiment count are unchanged by this wording correction.
- [ ] Confirm the sole manipulated variable in the core ladder is threshold-calibration scope.
- [ ] Confirm the confirmatory evidence is restricted to N-BaIoT natural physical-device clients, SHARED_THRESHOLD versus LOCAL_THRESHOLD, CV(FPR), ten paired seeds, locked BCa decision.
- [ ] Confirm every experiment has exactly one primary evidence role and cannot be promoted post hoc.
- [ ] Confirm supportive, mechanism, external, stress-test, boundary, and exploratory evidence remain subordinate to the confirmatory endpoint.
- [ ] Confirm the independent scientific replication unit is the training seed.
- [ ] Confirm false-alarm/operating-point equity language is used rather than demographic/protected-group fairness.
- [ ] Confirm AUROC remains a detector-quality control under fixed scores.
- [ ] Confirm negative trade-offs, especially lower-tail classification weakness, remain visible.
- [ ] Confirm all explicit non-goals and claim boundaries are preserved.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST B — Dataset integrity
- [ ] Verify exactly the roadmap-authorized datasets are used: N-BaIoT, CICIoT2023, Edge-IIoTset; no extra external IoT dataset is introduced.
- [ ] Verify N-BaIoT non-finite declared features fail validation rather than being filled.
- [ ] Verify CICIoT2023 canonical rows remain lossless and model-input eligibility requires recognized normalized label plus all declared model-input features finite.
- [ ] Verify CICIoT2023 gate records unrecognized/missing-label and non-finite-feature signals independently.
- [ ] Verify CICIoT2023 rows are never imputed, zero-filled, clipped, capped, infinity-replaced, or label-inferred.
- [ ] Verify Edge canonical lexical values/provenance are retained while model input uses exactly the locked 33 finite-numeric columns in canonical order.
- [ ] Verify Edge rows with null/non-finite retained numeric fields are excluded with provenance, never filled.
- [ ] Verify raw timestamps, labels, source folders, and client identity never enter Edge model input.
- [ ] Verify no Edge padding to 115 dimensions, truncation, silent 115-input weight reuse, or unvalidated categorical encoder.
- [ ] Verify every dataset-specific unavailable science is represented explicitly rather than fabricated.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST C — Population integrity
- [ ] Verify N-BaIoT natural population contains the nine physical devices and no outcome-informed filtering.
- [ ] Verify all nine N-BaIoT clients remain visible in mechanism reporting.
- [ ] Verify the 20-client Dirichlet population is synthetic and never replaces natural-device evidence.
- [ ] Verify CICIoT2023 uses 63 file-defined pseudo-clients only and never reconstructs the original 105-device topology.
- [ ] Verify no additional CICIoT2023 physical-device population (formerly the stale "Regime B-b" identity) is implemented or claimed; `CICIOT_FILE_CLIENTS` is the only authoritative CICIoT2023 population (resolves AMBIG-007).
- [ ] Verify Edge static external population uses ten audited benign sensor groups including Modbus.
- [ ] Verify Edge temporal population uses nine verified chronological groups and excludes Modbus for unusable timestamps.
- [ ] Verify family taxonomy is used only where defensible, stable, auditable, and independent of test outcomes/attack labels.
- [ ] Verify client membership is outcome-blind and row-conserving within its declared construction.
- [ ] Verify candidate, eligible, excluded, fallback, and attack-evaluable client counts are explicit.
- [ ] Verify no synthetic/pseudo-client population is used to claim real fleet-scale validation.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST D — Split integrity
- [ ] Verify calibration and evaluation rows are disjoint.
- [ ] Verify training/preprocessing fit uses only the declared training partition.
- [ ] Verify benign-only calibration semantics are preserved.
- [ ] Verify attack-labelled rows never enter threshold calibration.
- [ ] Verify identical split membership is reused across compared threshold policies.
- [ ] Verify temporal records are stably ordered by genuine capture time.
- [ ] Verify Edge temporal split is exactly 55% historical training, 15% historical calibration, 10% future recalibration, 20% future evaluation.
- [ ] Verify duplicate timestamps preserve original stable row order.
- [ ] Verify matched static temporal reference uses the same 55/15/10/20 row budget after deterministic client-local randomization.
- [ ] Verify the 10% static reserve is retained but not fit, scored, or evaluated and is not given false temporal meaning.
- [ ] Verify future evaluation cannot influence any earlier stage.
- [ ] Verify no pseudo-time or generated ordering substitutes for real chronology.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST E — Preprocessing integrity
- [ ] Verify every compared threshold policy reuses one fitted preprocessing state within seed/population/training baseline/named protocol.
- [ ] Verify FEDERATED_CLIENT_LOCAL_STANDARD uses StandardScaler with_mean=True, with_std=True, fitted client-locally on benign train only.
- [ ] Verify StandardScaler constant-feature rule uses unit scale for zero training scale and produces zero-centered column.
- [ ] Verify transformed values are retained unclipped.
- [ ] Verify fitted preprocessing persists via skops trusted estimator classes only.
- [ ] Verify reload transform equivalence absolute tolerance is 1e-12.
- [ ] Verify FEDERATED_POOLED_MIN_MAX is supportive only and cannot silently replace the confirmatory preprocessing geometry.
- [ ] Verify CENTRALIZED_POOLED_MIN_MAX is independent of all federated fitted states and maps zero training range to zero.
- [ ] Verify no missing-value imputation/zero-fill/capping/infinity replacement/label inference occurs.
- [ ] Verify cluster-fingerprint StandardScaler is score-side threshold preprocessing and never model-input preprocessing.
- [ ] Verify Edge 33-column feature order is part of preprocessing identity/checksum.
- [ ] Verify distinct preprocessing protocol identities are never mixed silently.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST F — Training integrity
- [ ] Verify core confirmatory training uses FedAvg, one local epoch per round, full participation, fixed model family/architecture contract, and paired seeds.
- [ ] Verify journal training evaluates only declared checkpoint candidates 25, 50, 75, 100, 125, 150, 200.
- [ ] Verify the journal maximum/terminal round is 200.
- [ ] Verify optimizer/loss/batch/weighting fields that are ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED are not silently invented as roadmap facts.
- [ ] Verify each training-side stress test trains its own models and score sets.
- [ ] Verify a separate FEDAVG detector (including IID) is trained per `(training seed, heterogeneity severity)` cell in the controlled non-IID experiment; population-dependent fitted preprocessing state, detector weights, checkpoint, calibration scores, and evaluation scores are never reused across severity cells (resolves AMBIG-003).
- [ ] Verify FedProx uses only the locked mu grid {0.001,0.01,0.1,1.0}; mu=0 is not a FedProx condition.
- [ ] Verify primary FedProx mu is selected only by lowest population-weighted terminal benign training loss at round 200 averaged across confirmatory seeds, tie smallest mu.
- [ ] Verify genuine Ditto maintains distinct global and persistent client-personalized states and the correct proximal personalized objective.
- [ ] Verify personalized states are never aggregated as global.
- [ ] Verify training-side stress tests are reported as sensitivities and cannot alter the FedAvg confirmatory ladder.
- [ ] Verify no training hyperparameter is selected from attack/test/CV(FPR)/external outcomes.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST G — Checkpoint integrity
- [ ] Verify anchor checkpoint semantics remain historical and are not retrofitted with the journal checkpoint rule.
- [ ] Verify the journal primary checkpoint round number is fixed at 200.
- [ ] Verify the same primary round number applies across applicable main regimes/policies where that checkpoint exists.
- [ ] Verify model weights remain seed-, population-, dataset-, and training-method-specific despite shared round number.
- [ ] Verify CENTRALIZED_REFERENCE uses its own candidate set and never consumes federated checkpoints.
- [ ] Verify no policy-specific checkpoint selection occurs.
- [ ] Verify no checkpoint is selected by test AUROC, FPR/CV(FPR), Macro-F1, BA, attack labels, threshold effect, external/stress-test outcomes, or policy-specific best performance.
- [ ] Verify non-terminal candidates remain stability evidence and are not suppressed.
- [ ] Verify detector/checkpoint identity is persisted sufficiently for downstream score identity proof.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST H — Score integrity
- [ ] Verify score generation uses the correct selected detector and fitted preprocessing identity.
- [ ] Verify calibration and held-out evaluation scores carry stable client/split/row identity.
- [ ] Verify the same calibration/test score artifacts are reused across core threshold policies.
- [ ] Verify threshold policies never regenerate or alter scores.
- [ ] Verify held-out labels remain attached to the same held-out score rows across policies.
- [ ] Verify higher reconstruction error always means greater anomaly evidence.
- [ ] Verify score comparison operator is fixed as attack when error > threshold, benign when error <= threshold.
- [ ] Verify all reported confusion counts come only from held-out test rows.
- [ ] Verify stress-test detectors generate separate score sets from FedAvg.
- [ ] Verify persisted/reloaded scores preserve values and row-label association at `NUMERICAL_RELOAD_EQUIVALENCE` (`1e-12`), which must never be promoted to policy-level `SCIENTIFIC_ARTIFACT_IDENTITY` (resolves AMBIG-004).

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST I — Calibration integrity
- [ ] Verify all core and DATP-compatible threshold variants use benign calibration data only.
- [ ] Verify canonical eligibility is n_k_source >= 100 benign calibration samples before test evaluation.
- [ ] Verify eligible population is identical across compared policies.
- [ ] Verify ineligible clients cannot silently enter primary CV(FPR).
- [ ] Verify any fallback is separately declared and only used in an explicit fallback experiment.
- [ ] Verify attack labels cannot influence q, eligibility, checkpoint, comparator tuning, shrinkage, conformal alpha, cluster K/features, or external client construction.
- [ ] Verify calibration-size subsamples are drawn without replacement and nested within training seed.
- [ ] Verify calibration subsample replicate count is exactly 10 per (training seed, client, size), selected deterministically from training_seed/client/replicate_index.
- [ ] Verify subsampling replicates do not increase the seed count.
- [ ] Verify future recalibration uses only its designated future benign window and precedes future evaluation.
- [ ] Verify the n_k_source/m distinction is applied consistently: canonical eligibility is fixed from `n_k_source >= 100` before subsampling, `(client, m)` feasibility is `n_k_source >= m`, and `m = 50` is a resolved sample-starved supportive/diagnostic condition that never redefines canonical eligibility (resolves AMBIG-002).

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST J — Threshold integrity
- [ ] Verify SHARED_THRESHOLD is arithmetic mean of eligible local q-quantiles and not the exact pooled quantile.
- [ ] Verify LOCAL_THRESHOLD is each eligible client's own q-quantile.
- [ ] Verify canonical q is 0.95.
- [ ] Verify FAMILY_THRESHOLD uses validated physical-device family membership and member local thresholds only.
- [ ] Verify CLUSTER_THRESHOLD fingerprint is exactly mean(error), std(error), skewness(error), p95(error).
- [ ] Verify canonical CLUSTER_THRESHOLD K is 3; alternative K remains exploratory.
- [ ] Verify CLUSTER_THRESHOLD cluster threshold is mean member local thresholds; optional median variant keeps assignments unchanged.
- [ ] Verify pooled shared quantile and sample-weighted shared threshold remain supportive controls.
- [ ] Verify fixed shrinkage formula and full lambda grid {0,0.25,0.50,0.75,1.00}.
- [ ] Verify size-aware lambda(n_k) is pre-specified, bounded [0,1], client-invariant except n_k, and compared with fixed-lambda curves.
- [ ] Verify split-conformal alpha=1-q and main alpha=0.05; exact rank rule remains ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED.
- [ ] Verify FEDERATED_BENIGN_SUMMARY_STATISTICS_THRESHOLD uses only benign summaries, full within+between pooled variance, matched target exceedance, and disclosed client statistics.
- [ ] Verify fixed-k summary sensitivity uses only {2.0,2.5,3.0} and is supplementary.
- [ ] Verify no threshold parameter is tuned from held-out attack/test metrics.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST K — Evaluation integrity
- [ ] Verify metrics are calculated per client before cross-client aggregation wherever valid client identity exists.
- [ ] Verify primary FPR equity aggregation is unweighted by client row count.
- [ ] Verify FPR denominator and typed unavailability rules.
- [ ] Verify TPR requires valid per-client attack assignment and non-empty attack denominator.
- [ ] Verify BA requires both FPR and TPR.
- [ ] Verify Macro-F1 computes benign and attack class F1 separately and never silently zeroes undefined class metrics.
- [ ] Verify AUROC uses continuous scores, both classes, and is policy-invariant under fixed scores.
- [ ] Verify CV(FPR) uses population SD ddof=0, no epsilon, and is undefined when mean FPR=0.
- [ ] Verify near-zero mean FPR triggers warning and absolute-dispersion interpretation.
- [ ] Verify IQR, range, worst FPR accompany CV where required.
- [ ] Verify attack aggregates report attack-evaluable client count.
- [ ] Verify Edge attack-sensitive per-client metrics are typed unavailable.
- [ ] Verify pooled controls never replace client-level operating-point results.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST L — Statistical integrity
- [ ] Verify training seed is the independent inferential unit.
- [ ] Verify paired policies are never resampled independently.
- [ ] Verify confirmatory point estimate is arithmetic mean of ten paired SHARED_THRESHOLD–LOCAL_THRESHOLD CV(FPR) deltas.
- [ ] Verify confirmatory interval is two-sided 95% BCa over paired seed deltas.
- [ ] Verify BCa resamples paired deltas with replacement and uses paired data for bias correction/acceleration.
- [ ] Verify degenerate BCa handling reports paired values/point estimate and does not silently substitute another confirmatory interval; the resolved outcome is `CONFIRMATORY_INFERENCE_UNAVAILABLE` (confirmatory claim NOT ESTABLISHED), never silently converted to `CONFIRMATORY_SUPPORT` or `NO_OBSERVED_ADVANTAGE` (resolves AMBIG-006).
- [ ] Verify sign consistency reports positive proportion plus zero/negative counts and remains descriptive.
- [ ] Verify Wilcoxon is paired, two-sided, explicit about zero differences, exact when possible, and secondary.
- [ ] Verify matched-pairs rank-biserial is used instead of unpaired Cliff's delta.
- [ ] Verify confirmatory endpoint receives no multiplicity correction.
- [ ] Verify emphasized secondary p-value families are pre-defined and Holm-corrected within family.
- [ ] Verify nested replicates are summarized within seed before across-seed inference.
- [ ] Verify heterogeneity association reports Spearman, declared regression, coefficient uncertainty, R², influence, all observations, and associative language.
- [ ] Verify cluster ARI is accompanied by assignments, sizes, empty/singleton status, and contingency tables.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST M — Experiment completeness
- [ ] Verify all 24 independently executable experiment/analysis specifications in this matrix are present.
- [ ] Verify each experiment has a descriptive stable ID and evidence role.
- [ ] Verify dataset/population/client count/eligibility/taxonomy/chronology/attack-evaluable status are recorded.
- [ ] Verify preprocessing, training method, detector/checkpoint, score reuse/regeneration, and calibration state are recorded.
- [ ] Verify the manipulated variable/grid and frozen state are explicit.
- [ ] Verify every comparator, threshold variant, training comparator, centralized comparator, and sensitivity factor is listed.
- [ ] Verify all applicable numerical constants reference the numeric ledger.
- [ ] Verify execution procedure is ordered from data through evidence/reporting.
- [ ] Verify experiment-specific invariants are explicit.
- [ ] Verify primary/supporting/control/diagnostic/unavailable metrics are listed.
- [ ] Verify statistical estimand/pairing/CI/correction/decision rule is listed where applicable.
- [ ] Verify expected intermediate/final artifacts are listed or marked ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED.
- [ ] Verify figure/table dependencies are listed or explicitly absent/unspecified.
- [ ] Verify allowed claims and forbidden stronger wording are explicit.
- [ ] Verify null/opposite/infeasible outcomes and scientific failure conditions are explicit.
- [ ] Verify every experiment ends with a tickable implementation-audit checklist.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST N — Anchor integrity
- [ ] Verify `anchor` retains the conference-faithful reference identity.
- [ ] Verify confirmatory procedure reproduces the locked five-seed subset using the journal implementation.
- [ ] Verify the five-seed reproduction is evaluated against the explicit fourteen-condition anchor reproduction gate (resolves AMBIG-005) before the ten-seed extension in procedure order.
- [ ] Verify historical anchor endpoint/checkpoint semantics are not retrofitted with journal round-200 selection.
- [ ] Verify confirmatory ten-seed result is allowed to be weaker/materially different and then becomes the main result.
- [ ] Verify the five-seed result is labeled preliminary if ten-seed evidence is weaker/materially different, and only after the gate has already passed.
- [ ] Verify the reference interval `[0.647, 0.769]`, width `0.122`, multiplier `1.20`, and operative maximum reproduced width `0.1464` (display `0.147`) are used exactly, with no invented additional equivalence margin.
- [ ] Verify all fourteen acceptance conditions are checked and that any single failure yields `ANCHOR_REPRODUCTION_FAILED`.
- [ ] Verify `ANCHOR_REPRODUCTION_FAILED` blocks the ten-seed extension and all downstream journal claim-generating execution, is never overridden by supportive/external/favorable-alternative evidence, and is never relaxed after observing the result.
- [ ] Verify the deterministic path `ANCHOR_REPRODUCTION -> ANCHOR_VERIFICATION -> ANCHOR_ACCEPTANCE_GATE -> JOURNAL_EXECUTION_ALLOWED / JOURNAL_EXECUTION_BLOCKED` has no undefined failure branch.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST O — Temporal integrity
- [ ] Verify temporal evidence uses only EDGE_TEMPORAL_GROUPS with genuine usable timestamps.
- [ ] Verify Modbus is excluded from temporal population for unusable timestamps.
- [ ] Verify stable chronological ordering and 55/15/10/20 split exactly.
- [ ] Verify preprocessing/model fitting has no future leakage.
- [ ] Verify historical thresholds use historical calibration only.
- [ ] Verify frozen-future state applies historical thresholds unchanged to future evaluation.
- [ ] Verify one-shot recalibrated state uses future recalibration only and the same future evaluation rows.
- [ ] Verify matched static reference uses same nine clients and row budget.
- [ ] Verify drift_excess and recovered_amount formulas exactly.
- [ ] Verify recovery_ratio is undefined unless drift_excess > materiality threshold 0.05.
- [ ] Verify meaningful recovery requires recovery_ratio >= 0.5.
- [ ] Verify temporal BCa resamples paired seed records, not rows/windows.
- [ ] Verify no outcome is framed as continuous/online/streaming/concept-drift solution.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST P — Artifact/provenance integrity
- [ ] Verify every artifact has producing stage, dataset/population/seed/experiment identity where applicable.
- [ ] Verify canonical data preserve row/source provenance.
- [ ] Verify eligibility/population/split manifests preserve exact identities and exclusions.
- [ ] Verify preprocessing state persistence is skops-only with trusted estimators and reload equivalence.

- [ ] Verify score artifacts identify detector/preprocess/split/client/row.
- [ ] Verify calibration subsample manifests reproduce deterministic row selection.
- [ ] Verify threshold artifacts identify estimator, q/parameters, scope, grouping, and input score/calibration identity.
- [ ] Verify evaluation artifacts preserve typed unavailability and denominator context.
- [ ] Verify inference artifacts preserve seed-level inputs and method identity.
- [ ] Verify Edge preprocessing checksum identity includes ordered 33-feature protocol even though hash algorithm is ROADMAP_UNSPECIFIED.
- [ ] Verify serialization/checksum/output layout choices not stated by roadmap are not misrepresented as scientific locks.
- [ ] Verify figure/table exports are reproducible from validated evidence.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST Q — Publication integrity
- [ ] Verify the confirmatory result is manuscript-visible regardless of sign/strength.
- [ ] Verify supportive evidence cannot replace a failed confirmatory endpoint.
- [ ] Verify null, opposite, unstable, and infeasible mandatory outcomes remain reportable.
- [ ] Verify lower P10 Macro-F1 or other negative trade-offs remain visible.
- [ ] Verify Edge attack-sensitive metrics are visibly unavailable, not omitted without reason.
- [ ] Verify CICIoT2023 wording remains file-pseudo-client-specific.
- [ ] Verify temporal claims remain one-shot/bounded.
- [ ] Verify privacy/deployment/fleet-scale/non-IID-solution claims remain prohibited.
- [ ] Verify estimated communication/storage/alert burden is labeled estimated and source assumptions disclosed.
- [ ] Verify every figure/table is traceable to valid experiment artifacts.
- [ ] Verify figure/table interpretation does not exceed evidence tier.
- [ ] Verify full precision is used for computation and rounding is presentation-only.
- [ ] Verify recommended presentation precision is applied where publication formatting is implemented.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST R — Numerical lock
- [ ] Verify every scientific numeric literal/spelled count used by implementation exists in the Numerical Constant Ledger.
- [ ] Verify every ledger value is used only in its documented scope/meaning.
- [ ] Verify q=0.95 canonical and q sensitivity grid are not conflated.
- [ ] Verify n_k_source >= 100 eligibility is not conflated with calibration-size ablation levels `m in {50,100,250,500,1000,5000}`; verify `(client, m)` feasibility uses `n_k_source >= m` and `m = 50` is never treated as a canonical-eligibility redefinition.
- [ ] Verify K=3 canonical cluster count and K=9 exploratory mention remain distinct.
- [ ] Verify checkpoint candidates and terminal 200 round exactly.
- [ ] Verify 10 calibration subsample replicates exactly.
- [ ] Verify FedProx mu grid and tie-break rule exactly.
- [ ] Verify Edge 33-feature projection and 33-25-17-11-8-11-17-25-33 architecture exactly.
- [ ] Verify temporal 55/15/10/20 split exactly.
- [ ] Verify temporal materiality 0.05 and minimum recovery ratio 0.5 exactly.
- [ ] Verify Ditto 0.75/0.25 absorption bands and 0.05 alternative-route threshold exactly.
- [ ] Verify presentation precision values affect display only, never calculations.

### GLOBAL CHECKLIST S — No scientific drift
- [ ] Verify detector identity cannot silently vary by threshold policy.
- [ ] Verify preprocessing protocol/state cannot silently vary by threshold policy.
- [ ] Verify client membership and eligibility cannot silently vary by policy or outcome.
- [ ] Verify split membership cannot silently vary by policy.
- [ ] Verify calibration benign-only semantics cannot silently change.
- [ ] Verify threshold estimator formula/scope/q/grouping cannot silently change.
- [ ] Verify score semantics and attack comparison operator cannot silently change.
- [ ] Verify metric formulas/ddof/undefined rules cannot silently change.
- [ ] Verify checkpoint selection cannot silently become test-driven or policy-specific.
- [ ] Verify seed cohort/pairing cannot silently change.
- [ ] Verify nested replicates cannot silently become independent replications.
- [ ] Verify statistical estimator/CI/test/multiplicity rules cannot silently change.
- [ ] Verify evidence tier cannot silently change after results.
- [ ] Verify claim wording cannot silently become stronger than the allowed evidence.
- [ ] Verify unavailable metrics cannot silently become zero/fabricated/inherited.
- [ ] Verify external dataset/client definitions cannot silently be reinterpreted.
- [ ] Verify chronology cannot silently be fabricated or reordered.
- [ ] Verify stress-test detectors/scores cannot silently be reused as core FedAvg evidence.
- [ ] Verify negative/null/opposite/infeasible results cannot silently disappear from reporting.
- [ ] Verify eligibility is never silently recomputed after calibration-size subsampling (i.e., `n_k_source >= 100` is fixed before `m`-sized subsampling; resolves AMBIG-002).
- [ ] Verify detector weights are never silently reused across different heterogeneity severities (resolves AMBIG-003).
- [ ] Verify supposedly identical fixed scores are never silently, independently regenerated by a threshold policy instead of reusing one `SCIENTIFIC_ARTIFACT_IDENTITY`-proven artifact (resolves AMBIG-004).
- [ ] Verify anchor acceptance is never silently weakened after observing results (the fourteen conditions and `0.1464` width bound are fixed before inspection; resolves AMBIG-005).
- [ ] Verify no statistical procedure is silently substituted for the locked BCa interval when it is unavailable (`CONFIRMATORY_INFERENCE_UNAVAILABLE`; resolves AMBIG-006).
- [ ] Verify an unsupported CICIoT2023 physical-device population is never silently resurrected or implemented (resolves AMBIG-007).

## 36. ROADMAP AMBIGUITY LEDGER

**Unresolved ambiguity count: 0.** All seven originally logged ambiguities were surgically resolved in the corrected Master Roadmap. This section is now a historical resolution log; none of the seven remain in an active unresolved state, and the corrected roadmap contains exactly one scientific interpretation for each.

| Ambiguity ID | Original conflict | Roadmap resolution | Resolution location | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AMBIG-001 | Declared count (five) conflicted with six enumerated programme-direction headings. | The roadmap now states "DATP-Core strengthens the original DATP study along six bounded directions," matching the unchanged six enumerated headings (§10.1–§10.6). No experiment, evidence tier, or scientific scope changed. | Scientific identity, scope, and claims > 10. Included scientific scope | RESOLVED |
| AMBIG-002 | Canonical `n_k >= 100` eligibility conflicted with the calibration-size ablation grid including `50`. | Two explicit quantities are now locked: `n_k_source` (source calibration support, canonical eligibility `n_k_source >= 100`, fixed before subsampling) and `m` (experimental calibration size, grid `{50,100,250,500,1000,5000}`). `(client, m)` feasibility requires `n_k_source >= m`; `m = 50` is an explicit sample-starved supportive/diagnostic condition, never a canonical-eligibility redefinition, and never enters the sole confirmatory endpoint. Cross-size comparisons use the feasible-client intersection. | Scientific identity, scope, and claims > 3.3 Client eligibility; Experiment programme and decision rules > 8.1 Calibration-size ablation | RESOLVED |
| AMBIG-003 | Unclear whether the controlled-heterogeneity experiment must train or may reuse a detector across Dirichlet severities. | A separate `FEDAVG` detector (including IID) is now required for every `(training seed, heterogeneity severity)` cell under a fixed training protocol. Population-dependent fitted preprocessing state, detector weights, checkpoint, calibration scores, and evaluation scores must never be reused across severity cells; within one fixed cell, all threshold policies reuse exactly the same frozen detector/checkpoint/preprocessing/scores/labels/eligibility. Cross-severity evidence is explicitly `SUPPORTIVE_ASSOCIATIVE`, not threshold-only causal. | Experiment programme and decision rules > 6.3 Controlled non-IID severity | RESOLVED |
| AMBIG-004 | Vague allusion to a "fixed-score absolute-tolerance magnitude" left the score/AUROC equality rule undefined relative to the `1e-12` preprocessing-reload tolerance. | A new `2.2.2 Fixed-score identity and serialization tolerance` subsection distinguishes `SCIENTIFIC_ARTIFACT_IDENTITY` (policy-level score/AUROC equality, proven by provenance) from `NUMERICAL_RELOAD_EQUIVALENCE` (`1e-12`, serialization/reload only). AUROC is now explicitly bound to the fixed score/label artifact; a policy-dependent AUROC difference is defined as a score/provenance identity failure, not a threshold effect. | Scientific identity, scope, and claims > 2.2.2; Evaluation, statistical analysis, and reporting > 4.5 AUROC | RESOLVED |
| AMBIG-005 | "Not materially inconsistent" anchor verification had no tolerance, statistic, pass/fail rule, or failure consequence. | A new `5.2 Anchor reproduction gate` locks the historical reference (`[0.647, 0.769]`, width `0.122`, multiplier `1.20`, maximum reproduced width `0.1464`/display `0.147`) and fourteen atomic acceptance conditions. Any failure yields `ANCHOR_REPRODUCTION_FAILED`, which blocks the ten-seed extension and all downstream journal claim-generating execution, is never overridden by supportive/external/favorable-alternative evidence, and is never relaxed after observing the result. Explicitly declared as a reproduction/compatibility gate, not a formal statistical equivalence test. | Experiment programme and decision rules > 5.2 Anchor reproduction gate | RESOLVED |
| AMBIG-006 | No explicit confirmatory verdict label existed for a degenerate/unavailable locked BCa interval. | A new `5.3 Confirmatory inference unavailable` defines `CONFIRMATORY_INFERENCE_UNAVAILABLE` (triggered by <10 valid paired deltas, undefined/invalid acceleration, degenerate bootstrap, or other detected degeneracy). The confirmatory claim is explicitly NOT ESTABLISHED; no secondary result, interval, or evidence family may substitute for it. | Experiment programme and decision rules > 5.3 Confirmatory inference unavailable; Evaluation, statistical analysis, and reporting > 11.3 Degenerate BCa | RESOLVED |
| AMBIG-007 | An additional listed regime identity (`Regime B-b`) had no corresponding population/dataset contract. | `Regime B-b` is removed from the regime-name list. The roadmap now explicitly states no additional CICIoT2023 physical-device population is defined; the available artifact supports `CICIOT_FILE_CLIENTS` only, and a future physical-device population would require independently verified device-level provenance plus an explicit roadmap revision. | Scientific identity, scope, and claims > 9.2 CICIoT2023 available-data boundary; > 12.6 Regime names | RESOLVED |
